title.narrative: Sustainable and regenerative management of rice production in Pakistan

description.narrative: 1. The project will ensure that project staff adhere to both national employment and labour laws, as well as international commitments, and will increase the protection and promotion of worker health and safety. 2. Changes in climate including changes in seasonal flow patterns in the Indus River, heat stress, increased evapotranspiration, and intensification of weather extremes have resulted in higher levels of vulnerability and potential for loss and damage. A major flooding event in 2022 resulted in more than 1.8 million hectares of agricultural land being damaged, and an estimated 80% loss of rice production (an estimated loss of 1.8 million tons of rice) in Sindh province alone. Rice is also a significant source of national methane emissions. As per the recent BUR, CH4 emissions from rice cultivation in Pakistan was 7.83 Mt CO2e accounting for 3.5% of the total emissions of the AFOLU Sector[1]. While rice alone contributes 0.7% of Pakistan’s GDP, the productivity of rice producers in Pakistan is low relative to other major rice producers in the region. Rates of poverty in agricultural regions are high and opportunities to diversify production landscapes by incorporating stress-tolerant varieties, sustainability practices throughout the value chain, and livelihood diversification through value chain development exist.3. The project will produce Global Environmental Benefits (GEB) by targeting sustainable and regenerative management of rice landscapes in Pakistan. To deliver GEBs, the project will drive transformative change toward sustainable rice production landscapes in Sindh Province, a major rice-producing area of Pakistan, and scale out this transformation through the National Food Security Policy (NFSP, 2018) as well as integration into private value chain and trade networks for sustainable rice and agriculture products.4. Through the enabling environment at national, provincial, and district scales for sustainable rice production landscapes, the project will promote sustainable rural livelihoods and employment, food security and nutrition, and facilitate restoration and resilience of agroecosystems. Public-private partnerships of this project will explore and develop market incentives and finance for rice and other products that can deliver environmental livelihood and employment benefits. Investment in nature-based solutions under this project will improve water management, reduce pollution, and conserve key sources of natural- and agro-biodiversity. Integrated landscape management coupled encompassing on-farm technologies and nature-based solutions will enable farmers to sustainably increase productivity and generate environmental, livelihood, and rural employment benefits. Climate-smart, agroecological, and regenerative production practices at scale through improved extension services and adoption of sustainability standards such as SRP will increase the reputation of Pakistan rice exporters, which will eventually increase the foreign earnings of the country. Adaptive knowledge management and outreach at national and global levels via engagement with relevant platforms will further strengthen collaboration with other developing countries through South-South and Triangular Cooperation mechanisms and share its knowledge and experience in sustainable agriculture and food systems with other countries.5. Hence, the project will ensure that the project staff adhere to both national employment and labour laws, as well as international commitments, and will increase the protection and promotion of worker health and safety. 6. Besides, the project has dedicated output on capacity building of women agri-entrepreneurs to engage in sustainable and resilient livelihoods (Output 3.2.2). Under this output, there will be capacity building and piloting activities of alternative livelihoods development, which will focus on vulnerable group including women and youth. To support the transition towards a sustainable, regenerative, and inclusive rice value chain that is nature-positive, resilient, and less pollution-intensive.
